ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a large rectangle divided into 7 squares. On the right side is a column of 3 gray diagonally striped squares stacked vertically; on the upper left side is a large white square; on the lower left side is a row of 3 equal small white squares. The width of the large white square is the same as the total width of the 3 small white squares below. Reasoning: Let the side length of each small white square be s. The side lengths of the gray squares are all 8, and the 3 gray squares on the right side are stacked vertically, so the height of the whole rectangle is 3×8=24. The height on the left side is composed of the side length of the large white square plus the side length of the bottom small white square. Since the width of the large white square equals the width of 3 small white squares, the side length of the large white square is 3s. Therefore the height of the rectangle is 3s+s=4s. Thus 4s=24, giving s=6. The side length of the large white square is 3s=18.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a big white square on the upper left, three equal small white squares along the bottom left, and three equal grey squares stacked on the right. Let the side of each small white square be s. From the text, each grey square has side 8, so the full rectangle height is 3×8=24. From the image, the big white square sits above the bottom row, so the rectangle height is also the big square side plus s. Also from the image, the big square’s width matches three small squares in a row, so its side is 3s. Thus the total height is 3s+s=4s=24, giving s=6 and the big white square side 3s=18.
